Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
225 PM EDT Wed Oct 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 222 PM EDT Wednesday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 222 PM EDT Wednesday...

1. Large ridge of surface high pressure will keep conditions 
dry with seasonable temperatures through the end of the week. 
There will be increasing fire weather concerns on Thursday into 
Friday with slightly stronger winds and low humidity values. 

2. Dry and seasonable conditions continue through the middle of
next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 222 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Our region remains under influence of surface 
high pressure even though the center of the ridge is shifting 
away from the area. There is also a low pressure system which 
continues to meander off the mid Atlantic and New England coast.
As the low moves northward and another ridge of high pressure 
builds into our area, will have increasing winds out of the 
north on Thursday. A weak surface front will also drop across 
our area on Thursday, but really only expecting an increase in 
clouds and no precipitation. Overnight minimum temperatures 
tonight will be highly dependent on elevation as a sharp low 
level thermal inversion develops with poor rh recoveries across 
the mid-upper elevations within this thermal belt. Lows will 
range from the mid 20s to mid/upper 30s with a sharp humidity 
range from excellent recoveries in the valleys to poor acrs the 
ridges. As the boundary approaches on Thurs, did note a slight 
increase in 925mb to 850mb moisture, along with a strengthening 
low level jet of 20 to 35 knots. Strongest winds appear to occur
btwn 00z and 12z Friday, when mixing profiles are less 
favorable, but expect localized gusty winds on ridges and Lake 
Champlain. Once again with developing winds poor rh recoveries 
are possible, especially summit level on Friday morning with a 
large spread in temps anticipated. Friday is the coolest day of 
the week with highs upper 30s to lower 50s acrs our region. Fire
weather concerns increase Thursday afternoon into Friday with 
slightly stronger surface winds, near critically dry humidities 
and recent dry spell resulting in receptive fine fuels, 
especially leaf litter. Winds and humidities will fall short of 
red flag conditions, but we will continue to monitor closely in 
the upcoming days ahead.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The classic stretch of fall weather will 
continue through the middle of next week. High pressure will 
shift to the east a bit for Sunday, and return southerly flow 
will cause temperatures to rise into the 60s for most places. A 
moisture starved cold front moves through Monday and Monday 
night, and while a brief sprinkle or mountain flurry is possible
during its passage, it will be pretty much completely dry. This
will drop highs back into the 50s and potentially upper 40s for
places Tuesday and Wednesday. While a prolonged stretch of dry 
weather will continue with some days of low relative humidity 
values, winds look to be too light to cause serious fire weather
concerns right now.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 18Z Thursday...VFR conditions are expected to prevail 
for the next 24 hours. The only exception would be tomorrow 
morning when brief MVFR ceilings could be possible. Winds will 
be mostly light/variable/terrain driven through tonight. Winds 
will increase a bit tomorrow morning after the passage of a cold
front and become northerly/northeasterly. Gusts in the 5-15 KT 
range are possible tomorrow, with the highest ones at BTV and 
PBG.

Outlook...

Thursday Night: VFR.
Friday: VFR.
Friday Night: VFR.
Saturday: VFR.
Saturday Night: VFR.
Sunday: VFR.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
